## Visa Guide for: United States of America
**Applicable to:** Indian Passport Holders Only
**Last Updated Officially On:** 1 October 2025 (Visa Integrity Fee and I-94 fee provisions, "One Big Beautiful Bill Act"/OBBBA take effect) / late 2025 (Interview Waiver Program eligibility narrowed)
**Information Status:** Current as of August 29, 2026

---

## Overview

### Country Information

-   **Country Name:** United States of America
-   **Region:** North America
-   **Capital:** Washington, D.C.
-   **Official Language:** English (no official language at federal level, but English is the de facto language of government and travel)
-   **Currency:** US Dollar (USD)
-   **Exchange Rate:** 1 USD = 95.4 INR (approximate)

> **Important:** The United States offers **no visa-free entry and no visa-on-arrival** for Indian passport holders — India is not part of the Visa Waiver Program (VWP/ESTA), which is limited to around 40 mostly European and East Asian partner countries. Every Indian traveler must obtain a visa in advance from a US Embassy or Consulate in India, regardless of trip length or purpose.

---

## Visa Type 1: B-1/B-2 Visitor Visa (Business & Tourism, Standard In-Person Route)

### Overview

The B-1/B-2 is the standard, combined business-and-tourism visa most Indian travelers apply for — B-1 covers business activities like meetings and conferences, B-2 covers tourism, family visits, and medical treatment, and consular officers typically issue both together as a single "B-1/B-2" stamp. Indian nationals typically receive the maximum available validity: **10 years, multiple entry**. However, the visa's validity is not your permitted stay — the Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer at the port of entry decides your actual authorized stay on each visit, commonly up to 6 months (180 days). This route requires the standard process: online application, biometrics at a Visa Application Center (VAC), and an in-person consular interview.

### Cost Structure

| Cost Component | Amount |
| :------------- | :----- |
| MRV Application Fee (non-refundable, paid to schedule the interview) | 185 USD (~17,650 INR) |
| Visa Integrity Fee (charged only if the visa is approved/issued; in effect for visas issued on or after 1 October 2025) | 250 USD (~23,850 INR) |
| I-94 Arrival Fee (land border crossings; most air/sea arrivals continue to use the free automated I-94 system — confirm current CBP guidance before travel) | 24 USD (~2,290 INR), where applicable |
| **Total Cost (Typical Air Arrival, Approved Applicant)** | **Approx. 435 USD (~41,500 INR)** |

> **Note on the Visa Integrity Fee:** This is a new, non-waivable $250 charge created by the "One Big Beautiful Bill Act" (signed 4 July 2025), applying to nearly all nonimmigrant visa categories including B-1/B-2. It is billed as theoretically refundable if the visa holder departs the US on time and doesn't violate visa conditions, but the refund mechanism was still being finalized as of mid-2026 — don't count on a quick or automatic refund. Applicants from Visa Waiver Program countries and most diplomatic visa holders are exempt; Indian B-1/B-2 applicants are not.

### Mandatory Document Requirements (Type 1)

1.  **Passport Details**
    *   **Validity:** Should be valid for the intended period of stay in the US (no fixed "6 months beyond stay" rule as with some countries, but longer validity is safer).
    *   **Pages:** At least 1-2 blank pages recommended.
    *   **Format:** Standard Indian passport.
2.  **Photograph (Digital)**
    *   **Size:** 2x2 inches (51x51mm); Background: White.
    *   **Quantity:** 1, uploaded with the DS-160 online application.
3.  **Travel Proof**
    *   **DS-160 Confirmation:** The mandatory online nonimmigrant visa application, completed at ceac.state.gov, generates a confirmation page/barcode required for your interview.
    *   **Itinerary:** A specific, credible travel plan — vague statements like "just want to visit" are a common cause of refusal; have concrete dates, destinations, and a clear return plan.
4.  **Additional Documents**
    *   **Financial Proof:** Bank statements and income documentation demonstrating sufficient funds and strong ties to India (property, family, employment) that support your intent to return.
    *   **Employment/Business Proof:** Employer letter or business registration documents, as applicable.
    *   **Prior Travel History:** Old passports showing previous international travel strengthen an application, though not mandatory.

**Current Appointment Wait Times (Highly City-Dependent — Check the Official Tracker Before Planning):**

| Consulate | Approx. First-Time B-1/B-2 Interview Wait (2026) |
|---|---|
| Chennai | Fastest, roughly 1-3 months |
| Hyderabad | Roughly 4.5-5.5 months |
| New Delhi | Roughly 4.5-5.5 months |
| Mumbai | Slowest, roughly 7-8 months |
| Kolkata | Roughly 4 months |

> Wait times fluctuate constantly with staffing, season, and demand — always check the live figures on the US Department of State's official wait-time page before booking flights, and apply at least 6-12 months ahead of your intended travel date.

---

## Visa Type 2: Interview Waiver Program (Dropbox Renewal — For Eligible Repeat Applicants)

### Overview

Applicants renewing the **same visa classification** (B-1/B-2 to B-1/B-2) can sometimes skip the in-person interview and simply submit ("drop box") their documents at a Visa Application Center. This has historically been the fastest route for repeat US travelers from India. However, the eligibility window was **sharply narrowed in late 2025** — previously covering renewals within 48 months of a prior visa's expiration, it now generally only covers applicants renewing within roughly **12 months** of their previous visa's expiration, with a clean record (no refusals, no overstays) and a full-validity prior visa. Many applicants who previously qualified for dropbox renewal now require a full in-person interview, which is part of why overall wait times rose through late 2025 and into 2026.

### Cost Structure

| Cost Component | Amount |
| :------------- | :----- |
| MRV Application Fee (same as Type 1) | 185 USD (~17,650 INR) |
| Visa Integrity Fee (on approval) | 250 USD (~23,850 INR) |
| **Total Cost** | **Approx. 435 USD (~41,500 INR)** |
| Processing Time | Typically weeks rather than months once documents are submitted, since no interview slot is needed |

### Mandatory Document Requirements (Type 2)

1.  **Eligibility Confirmation**
    *   Prior B-1/B-2 visa expired within approximately the last 12 months, issued for full standard validity, with no visa refusals or status violations on record — verify current eligibility criteria on your specific consulate's website, as this window is set centrally and can change.
2.  **DS-160 Confirmation**
    *   Same online application as Type 1.
3.  **Prior Visa/Passport**
    *   Original passport containing the previous US visa.
4.  **Updated Supporting Documents**
    *   Current employment/financial documents, even though a full interview isn't required — the consular officer still reviews the file.

---

## Visa Type 3: Other Nonimmigrant Visas (Student F-1, Work H-1B/L-1, Exchange J-1)

### Overview

For study, employment, or exchange programs rather than tourism/business. Student (F-1) visas require a SEVIS-registered school's Form I-20; work visas (H-1B, L-1, O-1, etc.) require an approved USCIS petition from a US employer before the consular visa stage; exchange visas (J-1) require a Form DS-2019 from a sponsoring program. These categories carry additional fees and, since December 2025, mandatory social media vetting has been reported at Indian consulates for employment-based categories specifically, which has added to processing times for that group.

### Cost Structure

| Cost Component | Amount |
| :------------- | :----- |
| MRV Application Fee | 185 USD (F-1/J-1); 190 USD (H, L, O and most other petition-based categories) |
| SEVIS Fee (F-1 students / J-1 exchange visitors) | 350 USD (F-1); varies for J-1 depending on program |
| Visa Integrity Fee (on approval) | 250 USD (~23,850 INR) |
| **Total Cost** | **Varies by category — commonly 600-800 USD (~57,000-76,000 INR), excluding any employer-side USCIS petition fees** |

### Mandatory Document Requirements (Type 3)

1.  **Sponsorship/Program Documents**
    *   **Student (F-1):** Form I-20 from a SEVP-certified US school, admission letter, proof of tuition/funding.
    *   **Work (H-1B/L-1/O-1):** USCIS Form I-797 approval notice for the underlying petition filed by the US employer.
    *   **Exchange (J-1):** Form DS-2019 from the sponsoring exchange program.
2.  **SEVIS Fee Receipt**
    *   Payment confirmation from the SEVIS I-901 system (F-1/J-1 categories), required before the visa interview.
3.  **Financial Proof**
    *   Sponsor's or applicant's financial documents demonstrating ability to cover tuition/living expenses (students) or standard supporting financials (work/exchange categories).
4.  **Social Media/Online Presence Disclosure**
    *   The DS-160 form requires listing social media handles used over the past 5 years; employment-based applicants should also be prepared for closer online-presence review as part of 2025-2026 vetting changes.

---

## Special Cases & Exemptions

-   **No Visa-Free Access for India:** The Visa Waiver Program (ESTA) is limited to roughly 40 partner countries (mostly Europe, Japan, South Korea, Australia, etc.) — India is not included, and there is no fallback visa-on-arrival option under any circumstance.
-   **Interview Waiver Narrowing (2025-2026):** As noted under Type 2, dropbox renewal eligibility shrank considerably in late 2025. If you're unsure whether you qualify, check your specific consulate's current interview waiver criteria before assuming you can skip the interview.
-   **Expedited/Emergency Appointments:** Available for documented medical emergencies, urgent business needs, or qualifying student/exchange visitor scenarios with imminent program start dates — requested through the online scheduling system with supporting evidence.
-   **Visa Extension/Change of Status:** Handled by USCIS from within the US (Form I-539 for most visitor extensions) — not something arranged at a port of entry or Indian consulate.

---

## Arrival Documentation

-   **Electronic I-94 (Arrival/Departure Record):** For most Indian travelers arriving by air or sea, the I-94 record is generated automatically by CBP at the port of entry — no paper form or separate fee in this case. It records your authorized stay date, which can differ from your visa's expiry date; check it via the official CBP I-94 website after arrival, since this date — not your visa's — governs how long you may legally stay.
-   **Customs Declaration:** Completed via the CBP mobile app (Mobile Passport Control / CBP One, depending on airport rollout) or a paper form in the arrivals hall; declare goods, food items, and cash equivalents over $10,000 as required.
-   **Visa Stamp vs. Status:** Remember your visa only gets you to the port of entry — the CBP officer's admission decision and the I-94 stay date are what actually govern your legal status during the trip.

---

## Comparison Table

| Feature | B-1/B-2 (Standard, In-Person) | Interview Waiver (Dropbox Renewal) | Other Nonimmigrant (F-1/H-1B/J-1) |
| :-------------------- | :-------------------- | :------------------------- | :---------------------------------- |
| **Total Cost** | ~435 USD (~41,500 INR) | ~435 USD (~41,500 INR) | ~600-800 USD (~57,000-76,000 INR) |
| **Stay Duration** | Up to 6 months per entry (CBP discretion), visa valid 10 years multiple-entry | Same as B-1/B-2 | Tied to program/employment (I-20, I-797, or DS-2019 validity) |
| **Where to Apply** | US Embassy/Consulate via VAC, in-person interview | VAC dropbox, no interview (if eligible) | US Embassy/Consulate, after underlying petition/admission approval |
| **Advance Planning** | Extensive — apply 6-12 months ahead given current wait times | Minimal once eligible — weeks rather than months | Extensive — petition/I-20/DS-2019 process itself can take weeks to months |
| **Best For** | First-time tourist/business travelers | Repeat travelers renewing the same visa class within the eligibility window | Students, employer-sponsored workers, exchange visitors |

---

**Disclaimer:** This guide provides general information for Indian passport holders. Always verify current requirements on official government websites (e.g., the US Embassy/Consulates in India at ustraveldocs.com, the US Department of State at travel.state.gov, or USCIS for petition-based categories) before applying, as fees — including the still-rolling-out Visa Integrity Fee — appointment wait times, and interview waiver eligibility have changed significantly since 2025 and may change again without prior notice.
